about.title: A more connected campus.
about.paragraph1: Today's university experience is spread across course calendars, learning systems, emails, spreadsheets, and club portals. Useful information can be difficult to find—and harder to connect.
about.paragraph2: Nexus aims to bring those workflows together for <emphasis>students, instructors, clubs, and university staff</emphasis>. The long-term vision includes degree planning, communication, campus resources, and support for multiple institutions.

planner.title: Introducing Course Planner.
planner.intro: More than a course catalog: a tool designed to help you understand how degree requirements and academic decisions affect what you can do next.
planner.feature1Description: Find course and program information, requirements, and electives in one place.
planner.feature2Description: See prerequisites, antirequisites, corequisites, and alternative course paths.
planner.feature3Description: Investigate what may still be possible after dropping, failing, or postponing a course.
planner.fineprint: Planned capabilities, not features available today. Scope may change during development.

roadmap.title: Development roadmap.
roadmap.intro: Nexus is being developed as a modular academic platform. Each phase builds toward a more connected university experience, beginning with the Course Planner.
roadmap.phase1Description: Academic data, prerequisite rules, degree progress, term planning, and what-if scenarios.
roadmap.phase2Description: Electron and React for Windows and macOS, with a unified dashboard and university resources.
roadmap.phase3Description: Course-based file organization, local storage, document previews, search, and note-taking.
roadmap.phase4Description: Chromium-based browsing, persistent sessions where supported, and authorized A2L and third-party integrations.
roadmap.phase5Description: Course material synchronization, document parsing, deadline extraction, and calendar exports.
roadmap.phase6Description: Context-aware academic assistance, local and cloud language models, and optional proactive workflows.
roadmap.phase7Description: Messaging, moderated forums, student communities, club management, and multi-university expansion.
roadmap.progressText: Initial McMaster academic data collection and SQLite storage are in place. Course planning logic and the first user interface remain under development.
roadmap.disclaimer: This roadmap represents long-term goals, not guaranteed features or release dates. Development priorities and technical implementations may change.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions.
faq.a1: An independent, student-built project exploring a connected academic and campus platform for students, instructors, organizations, and university staff.
faq.q2: Can it tell me which courses I can take if I fail one?
faq.a2: That is a central goal of the Course Planner. The feature is still in development and results will need to be checked against official academic rules.
faq.a3: The project starts with McMaster University because it is the institution the developer knows best. Multi-institution support is a long-term goal.
faq.q4: Is this an official university website?
faq.a4: No. Nexus is not affiliated with or endorsed by McMaster University or any other institution.
